definitions.explanation: Something or someone that serves as a standard to be copied or imitated. Used for both physical models (such as calligraphy samples) and ideal behavior.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}の{手本|てほん}を{見|み}て{書|か}く。
examples.english: To write while looking at the teacher's model.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{後輩|こうはい}の{手本|てほん}になる{社員|しゃいん}だ。
examples.english: She's an employee who serves as a role model for junior staff.

examples.japanese: まずは{手本|てほん}を{見|み}せますから、そのあと{同|おな}じようにやってみてください。
examples.english: I'll show you an example first, then please try to do it the same way.

notes:
WRITING:
{手|て} (hand) + {本|ほん} (book/origin). Originally referred to a copybook for practicing calligraphy or drawing.

USAGE:
Used both concretely (a physical model to copy from, as in calligraphy practice) and figuratively (a person or behavior to emulate). The phrase {手本|てほん}を{見|み}せる means "to set an example" or "to demonstrate."

{手本|てほん}になる (to serve as a model) can be either positive or negative depending on context — it usually implies a positive model unless qualified otherwise.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手本|てほん}を{見|み}せる: to show a model, to set an example
- {手本|てほん}にする: to use as a model
- {手本|てほん}になる: to serve as a model
- {良|よ}い{手本|てほん}: a good example
- お{手本|てほん}: model/example (polite)
